Subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU/APAC region availability

Hi Sofia 

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: Understand which deployment mode best fits NordBank for the Payments Insights product (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem).
- Key constraints you mentioned: EU data residency requirement for PII, some APAC traffic, and preference to avoid cross-region routing of sensitive logs.

Notes:
- Hosted API: fastest to get started; we have EU regions but it does rely on multi-region routing for some global failover options.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity in EU regions; better for predictable throughput and stronger isolation guarantees.
- Private VPC / On-prem: supports stricter network controls and can be deployed inside customer VPCs or on-prem for full residency and audit requirements.

Next steps I propose:
1) Aditya to confirm exact EU region availability and whether the Hosted API for NordBank can be scoped to avoid cross-region routing for logs and KV caches.
2) Share a short one-pager that compares Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private specifically for EU/ APAC residency (attached).
3) Schedule a 30-min technical session next week with your infra/security team to walk through networking and audit requirements.

Would Tuesday 2027-05-25 10:00 CEST or Wednesday 2027-05-26 14:00 CEST work for your team?


Lauren Bishop

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Thanks Lauren 

Adding technical detail on region/residency and routing. See inline answers to the items from the call:

- EU region availability: We currently have dedicated Hosted API endpoints in eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). For Dedicated we can provision reserved capacity in either region; provisioning lead time ~ 2-4 weeks depending on GPUs.

- Cross-region routing: By default our Hosted API uses region-aware routing with fallbacks. For NordBank we can create a configuration that restricts data plane traffic to keep inference requests and logs within the EU region (no egress to non-EU) - this requires an account-level policy and explicit routing rule, which we can enable before go-live.

- APAC traffic: For latency-sensitive APAC users, we recommend either: 1) provision regional Dedicated capacity in APAC for peak traffic, or 2) use Hosted API in EU with an APAC edge and caching for non-sensitive tokens (but that does involve cross-region edge nodes - not recommended for PII).

- Private VPC/on-prem: Full control over egress, logs, and KMS. If NordBank needs on-prem, we have an on-prem installer and a Private control plane option; this is by far the lowest surface for cross-region exposure but requires procurement and security signoff.

I'll attach the EU region availability datasheet and a short checklist of what we need from your infra team (VPC CIDRs, KMS approach, audit/log retention).

Note: Marissa is copied to help coordinate Dedicated sizing and SLA options.


Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachment: eu-region-availability-datasheet.xlsx

Thanks for the clear recap and detail. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Residency: NordBank requires that any PII and logging for EU customers remain in the EU. We also need proof points (SOC2, data flow diagrams) that show no cross-border egress for those datasets.

2) APAC: We expect low volume from APAC, so a caching/edge approach is fine for non-PII. For PII we want EU-only processing.

3) Timeline & procurement: Our security team wants to review the Private VPC option, but Procurement wants the Hosted vs Dedicated cost comparison first.

Can you share the SOC2 section that pertains to data processing locations and a sample network diagram showing how the Hosted API restricted routing would work? Also agree on a technical session - Wednesday 2027-05-26 14:00 CEST works for our infra/security team.
